# Remedy Sheet #4 — Vision prompt  ✅ researched, direction confirmed

`core/prompts.py::VISION_GENERIC`, `engines/instagram/prompts.py::IG_VISION`, and the generated `visionPrompt` from `campaign_gen.generate_advanced_prompts`.

**Researched 2026-08-21.** Every external claim below carries that date; ⚠️ marks anything not verified by executing repo code — re-verify before coding against it.

## The disease (verified in code)

- **The tier is dead on shipped defaults.** `_DEFAULT_VISION_MODEL = "nex-agi/nex-n2-pro:free"` (`core/router.py:337`) and `OPENROUTER_VISION_MODEL=nex-agi/nex-n2-pro:free` (`.env.example:21`). ⚠️ Live fetch of `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` on 2026-08-21 returned 419 models; **neither `nex-agi/nex-n2-pro:free` nor the text default `openrouter/owl-alpha` is in it**, while the paid `nex-agi/nex-n2-pro` and `nex-n2-mini` are. A retired id returns 404, which is in `_FATAL_STATUS_HINT` (`router.py:81-85`) → `_TerminalProviderError` → `_degrade`. Corroborated in-tree independently of the fetch: `router.py:83-84` already ships a 404 hint telling operators to check these two env vars against `/api/v1/models`, and `memory/known-issues.md:1547-1550` already records both defaults as dead ids.
- **The dead ids live in SIX places, and the router's are the two that don't matter.** `router.py:366-370` resolves `text_model or AIZU_TEXT_MODEL or OPENROUTER_TEXT_MODEL or _DEFAULT_*` — an explicit arg always wins, and both real execution paths pass one. `cli.py:1013`/`:1015` hardcode the dead ids as argparse defaults and `cli.py:134-135` passes them in explicitly, so `aizu run` and the panel Run button never touch the router default. Same for the whole worker fleet: `worker/config.py:299-300`, `:361-363`, `:416-417`, injected at `config.py:455-456`. A third copy sits at `engines/warming/tg_relevance.py:32` (`DEFAULT_GATE_MODEL`). Plus `.env.example:20-21` and the stale `CLAUDE.md:51`. **Fixing `router.py` alone changes nothing for any live box.**
- **`classify_image` is the only `classify_*` path with neither JSON mode nor the malformed-200 guard.** `router.py:868` calls `self._post(payload, budget=self._new_budget())`; `classify_text` calls `_post_verdict(...)` at `:706`/`:721`. `_post_verdict` (`:536-584`) exists *specifically* because of the 2026-08-19 IG shakedown where 3 of 12 reels returned HTTP 200 with prose, and `_decision_from_payload` (`:285-302`) manufactured `label="unknown" score=0.00 confidence=0.00 tier="cloud"` — a confident reject `_unsure` cannot detect. That bug is still live on the vision path, and vision is where it hurts most: on the thin-caption branch it is the sole judgment.
- **The vision tier's read-out is thrown away — which is *why* this input is un-benchmarkable.** Every vision prompt requires `"reason":"what on-screen text you read + verdict"` (`core/prompts.py:41`; `IG_VISION`; `config/campaigns/tashkent-renovation.md`). `grep -n 'ocr_text\s*=' engine/aizu/` returns only `cli.py:84`, `cli.py:95` (demo fixtures) and the COALESCE at `store.py:1659`. `Reel.ocr_text` (`core/feed.py:35`) is therefore always `""`, so `mark_seen(..., ocr_text=reel.ocr_text or None)` (`instagram/session.py:604`, `x/session.py:468`, `linkedin/session.py:431`) always writes NULL. Confirmed against the dev DB: 0 rows with non-empty `ocr_text`. Two consequences beyond the missing corpus: `_comment_content`'s `"on-screen text: …"` block (`instagram/cascade.py:109-110` + twins) never populates, so the match stage never sees what vision read; and `panel.py:239` ships an always-empty `ocrText` to the operator.
- **The verdict is un-attributed.** `used_vision` is set at `instagram/cascade.py:252`/`:271` and returned at `:333`; **no session or store reads it.** `Cascade` carries `self.escalations` (`:169`) and `self.video_analyses` (`:171`) but no vision counter, though the *rarer* video tier has one. `classify_image` receives `stage="relevance"` (`:250`, `:269`) or `"video_analysis"` (`:307`), so `spend_log.stage` never contains `"vision"` despite the schema comment reserving it (`store.py:267`). The only discriminator left is the `model` column, and `.env.example:31-34` explicitly recommends one VL model for both. And `_record` writes a row only when `usd > 0` (`router.py:636`) — so under the shipped **free** default every vision call is invisible in the ledger by construction.
- **The final escalation discards the vision verdict** and, on the thin-caption path, asks a TEXT model to judge an empty string. `instagram/cascade.py:321-325` overwrites `d` with `classify_text(content=f"[ESCALATED]\nCAPTION:\n{reel.caption}")` — no `ocr_text`, no `transcript`, no `video_analysis`, no frames. The thin-caption branch (`:244-252`) fires precisely when the caption carries <6 word chars. Identical at `x/cascade.py:176-181`, `linkedin/cascade.py:176-181`. The match-side escalation at least carries the full `content` (`:356`).
- **Whether vision wins is decided by comparing two different models' self-reported confidence.** `instagram/cascade.py:272-273` `if dv.confidence >= d.confidence: d = dv` (and `:312-313` for video; `x/cascade.py:171-172`; `linkedin:171-172`). The text verdict comes from `text_model`, the vision verdict from `vision_model` — different calibration, and `>=` means a **tie goes to vision**. Sheet #3's research puts verbalized-confidence calibration error at ~45%. Nothing anywhere evidences that these two numbers are comparable.
- **`_unsure` gates the RELEVANCE tier on the MATCH threshold.** `instagram/cascade.py:160` `return abs(decision.score - campaign.threshold) < 0.05`, while the relevance decision is taken at `RELEVANCE_GATE = 0.5` (`:37`, applied at `:327`). With the shipped Tashkent brief (`threshold: 0.70`) a relevance score of 0.50 — dead on the real boundary — is *not* unsure, while 0.72 *is*. This clause is one of the two triggers deciding whether vision runs at all, so the tier fires on the wrong population. The same body is duplicated in all six engines: `instagram:150`, `x:103`, `linkedin:101`, `reddit:90`, `telegram:89`, `youtube:89`.
- **Two of the three vision-capable engines have no vision prompt at all.** `engines/x/cascade.py:129` `vision_system = self.campaign.vision_prompt or X_RELEVANCE`; `linkedin/cascade.py:129` `... or LINKEDIN_RELEVANCE`. `engines/x/prompts.py` defines only `X_RELEVANCE:15` and `X_MATCH:31`; `engines/linkedin/prompts.py` only `LINKEDIN_RELEVANCE:14` and `LINKEDIN_MATCH:30`. A panel-authored X or LinkedIn campaign with a blank vision prompt sends the model a system prompt describing how to judge post *text*. Exactly the bug Sheet #3 fixed for Instagram (`IG_VISION`), left unfixed on its twins.
- **The generated `visionPrompt` is validated for a JSON contract and nothing else.** `_prompt_carries_contract` (`campaign_gen.py:883-889`) checks `len >= 80`, `"json" in low`, `'"score"' in text`, `'"label"' in text` — the *same* predicate for all three keys (`_PROMPT_KEYS:879`, applied at `:917-918`). A model that emits the relevance prompt verbatim under `visionPrompt` passes. Nothing checks it mentions frames, on-screen text, multiple frames of one item, or the borderline-abstain convention that makes the confidence tie-break survivable.
- **The generator is told to write a vision prompt under a third the length of the one that works, and is never told the campaign's languages.** `SYSTEM_CAMPAIGN_PROMPTS` (`core/prompts.py:138-153`) says "Keep each prompt under 1200 characters" and describes the vision job in one clause. The hand-written Tashkent `## Vision Prompt` measures **4,261 characters** (measured), against `IG_VISION` ≈926 and `VISION_GENERIC` ≈714 — and nearly all its value is in the two things the generator is never asked for: enumerated hard negatives (auto/phone/watch repair, rental and sale cards, courses, materials retail — all containing РЕМОНТ and a price) and script/orthography notes (`қ ў ғ ҳ` dropped on a Russian keyboard, `ta'mir/taʼmir/tamir`). `_advanced_prompts_user` (`:892-900`) passes platform/objective/relevanceDef/matchDef/extractDef and **not `languageMix`**.
- **No threshold templating on the vision side.** `IG_VISION` and `VISION_GENERIC` (`core/prompts.py:32-42`) both hard-code `score>=0.50` in prose; the gate is the module constant `RELEVANCE_GATE = 0.5`. They agree by luck, and a generated prompt is free to state any cutoff with nothing checking it.
- **Frames are three near-identical stills from a 1.2-second window, and on non-video surfaces they are literally identical.** `capture_frames(reel, n=3, interval=0.6)` (`core/cdp.py:1035-1047`) calls `_shoot` three times 0.6s apart; `_shoot` (`:1003-1029`) does `page.query_selector("video")` then `el.screenshot(type="jpeg")` **else `page.screenshot(type="jpeg")`**. No seek to t=0, no time-spreading. On an X image post or a LinkedIn carousel there is no `<video>`, so the tier pays 3× for three byte-similar viewport screenshots including the platform's global nav — while the system prompt asserts frames are "from the same reel at different moments." The expensive tier does it properly (`sample_frames`, `core/media.py:135-154`).
- **No resize, no JPEG quality, no viewport pin.** `_shoot` takes `type="jpeg"` with no `quality=`, and there is no `set_viewport_size` anywhere in `core/cdp.py` or `instagram/cdp.py`. `scripts/warm_chrome.sh:393-397` launches Chrome with four flags — no `--window-size`, no `--force-device-scale-factor`; `worker/chrome_manager.py:379-382` builds the same argv. Payload size is a property of the operator's monitor.
- **The video-analysis tier ships PNG bytes labelled as JPEG.** `extract_frames` writes `frame-%04d.png` (`core/media.py:108`); `frames_to_base64` (`:157-169`) base64s the raw file and its docstring says the vision call adds the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` prefix; `router.py:851-853` duly does. Providers that sniff magic bytes tolerate it; providers that validate the declared mime 400.
- **Zero image fixtures, and the only executable vision path is a constant.** No `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp` exists anywhere in the repo. `scripts/eval/` has `variants/` (6 match) and `variants_relevance/` (3) and no vision variants; `gold.json` (25) and `gold_relevance.json` (20, **all `lang: "en"`** — measured) are text-only. `MockRouter.classify_image` (`core/mock_router.py:91-96`) returns a hard-coded `Decision(label="relevant", score=0.6, confidence=0.7, reason="mock OCR")` **ignoring both `images_b64` and `system`** — so every `--dry-run` and every test through the vision tier confirms nothing. Worse, 0.7 ≥ the top of the default escalate band `[0.4, 0.75]` (`core/config.py:372`) in most cases, so mock vision reliably wins the tie-break: dry-runs systematically overstate the tier.
- **Forty recorded runs, zero real vision calls.** The 40 parseable summaries in `engine/run-logs/*.log` aggregate to 99 `reels_seen`, 56 `relevance_passes`, 84 `matches` and `spend_usd` **0.00 in every one**; two carry `error: No LLM backend configured`. There is no historical vision verdict in this tree to benchmark against, and no persisted frame — `capture_video_frames` holds base64 in memory and sweeps its `MediaWorkdir` on exit by design (`engines/instagram/cdp.py:311-341`).
- **The video tier's instruction is doubled and its transcript is invisible to the system prompt.** `_video_instruction` (`instagram/cascade.py:76-92`) builds `relevance_def` + a `FRAME n @ Xs` roster + `SPOKEN TEXT (from audio)`; `classify_image` then appends its own hard-coded *"Read the on-screen text across these {n} frame(s) of the same reel and judge relevance"* (`router.py:846-849`) — a second, narrower instruction contradicting the roster. Meanwhile the system prompt in force never mentions a transcript and instructs a borderline 0.40-0.55 score "if there is little or no legible text" — so a reel with a rich transcript and a clean textless interior shot is told to abstain despite carrying the strongest evidence in the pipeline.
- **`_is_thin_caption` counts digits**, so the exact case the shipped brief names as vision's reason to exist routes to the text model. `instagram/cascade.py:44-51` strips `[#@]\w+` then requires ≥6 word-chars. The Tashkent vision prompt says a large share of genuine Uzbek renovation reels have an empty or **phone-number-only** caption. `+998 90 123 45 67` has 11 word-chars → not thin → the text branch, where vision runs only if `_unsure` fires (and that clause is misaimed).

## What is NOT wrong — two hazards already fixed, do not re-litigate

The obvious wall-clock story is false against the current tree, and recording it would send a build after a solved problem.

- **`per_reel_seconds = 90.0` (`core/cdp.py:122`) does NOT bound classification.** `reel_start` is anchored **after** `cascade.gate_reel()` returns — `instagram/session.py:626`, `x/session.py:482`, `linkedin/session.py:445` — under a "FIX P0" comment recording that the pre-fix ordering permanently blacklisted a relevant reel (`DFdnoSsgWBk`, 2026-08-19) whose classification overran. The backstop now bounds browser work only. No vision call is charged against it.
- **The 5-call chain vs the 180s watchdog is bounded by `_HeartbeatRouter`** (`instagram/session.py:91`, `x/session.py:69`, `linkedin/session.py:61`), which bumps `sessions.last_activity_at` in a `finally` around every model call. Its own docstring names the incident: bumping only on cascade return "multiplies whatever budget the router allows one call by five — and on 2026-08-20 that product killed job-2099fb29e88b five times over with 'stalled: no activity for over 180s'" (`session_watchdog.py:51` `STALL_TIMEOUT_SEC = 180`). The gap is now one bounded call: 100s (`router.py:117-122`) against 180s.
- A per-stage vision latency line already exists at `router.py:881` (`latency=%.0fms frames=%d`, debug).
- **The tier is not un-RUN as code.** `capture_fn` is wired on all three engines (`instagram/session.py:580`, `linkedin:410`, `x:447`) and `gate_reel` invokes `classify_image` on both the thin-caption path (`:252`) and the unsure path (`:266`). Whether it fired on any live box is a separate empirical question that is currently **unanswerable** — which is itself the defect.

## Remedy A — Un-brick the tier (model ids + verdict contract)

1. **Replace the dead ids in all six places**, not two: `router.py:336-337`; `cli.py:1013`, `:1015`; `worker/config.py:299-300`, `:361-363`, `:416-417`; `engines/warming/tg_relevance.py:32`; `.env.example:20-21`; plus the stale `CLAUDE.md:51`. Better than swapping literals: **delete the CLI/worker hardcodes** so `default=None` falls through to the router's single resolution chain — one place a dead id can live. This also fixes a latent bug: the CLI's explicit pass makes `AIZU_TEXT_MODEL` (`router.py:366`, the local-Ollama knob) unreachable on the CLI path.
   ⚠️ Live candidates with per-1M pricing read from `/api/v1/models` on **2026-08-21 — re-verify before coding**: `qwen/qwen3-vl-32b-instruct` in=$0.104 out=$0.416 (131k ctx, `response_format` + `structured_outputs`); `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` in=$0.300 out=$2.500 (1.05M ctx, `response_format` yes); `nex-agi/nex-n2-mini` in=$0.025 out=$0.100 (`response_format` yes); `nex-agi/nex-n2-pro` in=$0.250 out=$1.000 (**`response_format` NOT supported**). Free vision ids present today: `dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free` (`response_format` yes), `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` (yes, no structured outputs), `nvidia/nemotron-nano-12b-v2-vl:free` (**`response_format` NOT supported**).
2. **Add an id-resolution preflight row — but note it is greenfield.** `aizu/worker/preflight.py` makes **no** outbound call anywhere (no httpx/urlopen/http.client/socket), and its docstring promises testability "with no real browser, no network and no keychain"; `check_llm_backend` (`:759-794`) is a pure env predicate, **not** this shape of check. It must be a new probe injected through the `Probes` seam, returning `STATUS_UNKNOWN` on timeout per the module's "a timeout is not a refusal" rule (`:28-30`) and `STATUS_FAIL` only on an authoritative listing that omits the id. And `run_preflight` is called only from `worker/sidecar.py:729`, so a worker row does not cover `aizu run`/`run-all` or `server.py:3162/3208` — the local-first path. Cover those with a one-shot check in `cli._build_run_io` beside the existing `No LLM backend configured` guard (`cli.py:118-123`).
3. **Route `classify_image` through `_post_verdict`** instead of `_post` (`router.py:868`) so a verdictless 200 degrades and escalates instead of becoming a silent score=0.00 reject. `_post_verdict` (`:536-584`) already handles the label/score shape vision returns, and its parse-retries draw on the same `_CallBudget`, so the multiplication bug cannot return.
   ⚠️ **Do NOT add `response_format={"type":"json_object"}` as a two-liner.** `classify_image` (`:834-880`) has **no param-rejection handling**; the `_json_mode = False` latch-off plus stripped retry exists only in `classify_text` (`:707-725`) and `generate_json` (`:919-930`). A vision model that rejects the param would degrade on the first call and, since `self._json_mode` is never cleared from that path, on every subsequent vision call — and 400 is not in `_FATAL_STATUS` (`:79-86`), so each rejection burns `_post`'s full 3-attempt ladder plus backoff first. Two of the live candidates above do not advertise `response_format`. Either skip it for vision and rely on `_post_verdict` + the tolerant `_extract_json`, or mirror `classify_text` exactly (hoist `budget = self._new_budget()` into a variable, wrap in `_looks_like_param_rejection` → latch-off → `payload.pop("response_format")` → same-budget retry) gated on the model's advertised support.
4. **Fix the escalation cutoff — it is not one line and not one file.** `_unsure` is SHARED by both stages: Instagram calls it at `:264`, `:280`, `:300`, `:316` (relevance) and `:349` (match); ~17 call sites across six engines. Hardcoding `RELEVANCE_GATE` there would silently change match escalation too. Parameterize: `_unsure(decision, campaign, *, cutoff)`, relevance sites passing `RELEVANCE_GATE`, match sites passing `campaign.threshold`. **Scope honestly:** this changes only *when an escalation call is spent*, not the verdict — the relevance verdict already uses `RELEVANCE_GATE` (`:327`) and ignores score entirely when the model returns a relevant/irrelevant label. It is measurement hygiene, not part of un-bricking.

**Effort:** 1–1.5 days. **Risk:** low; the model swap changes cost from $0 to ~$0.0004/reel (Remedy J).

## Remedy B — Persist what vision reads (the enabler, ~15 lines)

Assign the vision verdict's read-out to `reel.ocr_text` at each of the three `classify_image` call sites (`instagram/cascade.py:248-252`, `267-273`, `305-313`; `x/cascade.py:147-172`; `linkedin/cascade.py:147-172`), exactly as the STT tier already does for `reel.transcript` at `instagram/cascade.py:134`. Column, write path and panel field are all wired end-to-end already (`core/feed.py:35` → `session.py:604` → `store.py:168` → `panel.py:239`); the only missing statement is the assignment. Prefer a dedicated `read_text` key over `Decision.reason` (Remedy G) and fall back to `reason` when absent, since `_decision_from_payload` truncates `reason` to 500 chars (`router.py:296`).

Also: turn `RelevanceResult.used_vision` (`:333`) into a `Cascade.vision_calls` counter beside `video_analyses` (`:171`) and into the run summary, and pass `stage="vision"` (or a substage) into `_record` so `spend_log.stage` finally means what its DDL comment says.

This makes every live run a growing, free, legally clean corpus of `{campaign, reel_id, caption, vision read-out, vision score, final relevant}` — **derived text, not a reproduction** — and simultaneously fixes the always-empty `on-screen text:` block in the match prompt.

**Effort:** 0.5 day. **Risk:** low. One caveat worth a test: an unparsed vision reply yields `reason=""`, so `ocr_text` must stay NULL rather than be written as an empty string (the COALESCE at `store.py:1659` already protects a later good read).

## Remedy C — Evaluate with NO labels: the image-ablation grounding test (the headline)

Run the same vision prompt twice per item — once with the frames, once with them removed (system prompt and instruction byte-identical) — and compare the two verdict distributions. If dropping the image barely moves score/label, the "vision tier" is a language prior wearing a camera and no prompt tuning will help. Report mean |Δscore|, label-flip rate and per-slice flip lists through `core/evalstats.py`, which Sheet #3 already built with Wilson intervals and exact McNemar over paired discordant counts — this is a paired design on the same items, exactly what that module measures.

Third variant worth the extra call: a **mismatched** frame (frames from a different reel with the same caption). A prompt returning the same verdict for the right and wrong image is not reading.

⚠️ Direct precedent: arXiv:2605.27750, *"Reading or Guessing? Visual Grounding Failures of Vision-Language Models for OCR"* (submitted 2026-05-26) introduces token-level grounding measures based on conditional-versus-image-free decoding distributions and finds VLMs "generate plausible but visually unsupported text, suggesting reliance on language priors," with prior-reliance being model-specific. arXiv:2509.10345 adds the mechanism — visual dependence decays as more tokens are generated — which is why Remedy G puts the transcription first. Abstracts fetched 2026-08-21; **re-verify before coding against them.**

Cost: 2–3× N calls at ~$0.0004 each — 200 items ≈ $0.25. Zero human labelling.

**Effort:** 1–1.5 days on top of Sheet #3's store-less real-router replay. **Risk:** medium-low. Two traps from Sheet #3: build ONE router per variant (`_json_mode` and `_degraded` are per-router latches) and abort any run that degrades. One vision-specific: an image-free `classify_image` short-circuits at `router.py:842-843` (`no frames to read` → degrade), so the ablation arm must send a blank frame, not an empty list.

## Remedy D — A pseudo-gold set for free: the held-out-caption trick

The population that needs vision (thin caption) is the population with no text label. But the population with a RICH caption has a cheap, defensible label — the text verdict from the caption, at high confidence, outside the escalate band. So: on those reels, capture frames anyway, run the vision prompt with the **caption withheld**, and score vision against the text verdict. Hundreds of labelled image items per run for a screenshot and a $0.0004 call, zero human labelling, zero image retention (store only the derived read-out per Remedy B).

It measures the exact quantity that matters — *when the answer is knowable, does the frame alone get there?* — and it transfers: a vision prompt reaching 0.85 agreement on rich-caption reels is the best available evidence it is not guessing on thin-caption ones. Stratify by declared language slice (uz-Latin / uz-Cyrillic / ru / mixed) and enforce Sheet #3's ≥30-per-slice rule, which `evalstats` already flags.

Complement with two things the DB can tell you once B lands: `vision_flip_rate` (of reels where vision ran, how often it flipped the text verdict) and, joined to `matches`, whether flipped-to-relevant reels actually produced leads — per-source yield is the precedent (`source_stats`, Sheet #1).

**Effort:** 2 days (capture-on-rich-caption is an opt-in flag on the gate; scoring is `evalstats`). **Risk:** medium — the label is a model verdict, so this measures **agreement, not truth**, and inherits the text prompt's biases. It can never certify vision as *better* than text, only as not-worse. Say that in the report rather than letting an agreement number read as accuracy. It also costs an extra screenshot + call on reels that did not need vision, so it belongs behind a flag.

## Remedy E — OCR as a VERIFIER and a GATE, never as the classifier

The direct question — does OCR-then-text-classify beat a VLM call here — resolves to **no**. ⚠️ But **not for character-dictionary reasons**: an earlier pass checked the wrong (PP-OCRv3-era) files and concluded three of the four Uzbek-Cyrillic letters were unemittable. That is false, and the correction matters because recording it would permanently exclude two usable engines and carry a wrong licence into dependency review.

What is actually true about Uzbek coverage (all fetched 2026-08-21 — **re-verify**):
- **PaddleOCR CAN emit Uzbek Cyrillic.** The current default line routes Cyrillic langs to `cyrillic_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec`, whose `ppocrv5_cyrillic_dict.txt` (850 entries) contains Ққ Ғғ Ҳҳ Ўў — verified on `main` and shipped v3.7.0. The legacy `cyrillic_dict.txt` (163 entries, missing қ ғ ҳ) is reachable only via an explicit `ocr_version="PP-OCRv3"/"PP-OCRv4"`. ⚠️ **The real trap is lang-code routing:** `paddleocr/_utils/langs.py:57` puts `uz` in `LATIN_LANGS`, so `PaddleOCR(lang="uz")` silently gets PP-OCRv6_medium_rec, whose 18,708-entry dict has **zero** Cyrillic. Use a Cyrillic lang code (`kaa`/`tg`/`kk`/`ru`) with `ocr_version="PP-OCRv5"`.
- **EasyOCR can too.** `cyrillic_g2`'s trained alphabet (`easyocr/config.py:206`) ends `…ЎўЏџҐґҒғҚқҮүҲҳҶҷ…`, and `easyocr/character/tjk_char.txt` contains all four including Ў/ў. `uz` being Latin-only in `latin_lang_list` is a routing fact, not a capability limit.
- **Tesseract** has genuine uz models (`uzb.traineddata` + `uzb_cyrl.traineddata`, verified present in `tessdata_best`) but is a **document** engine.
- **Surya** is **Apache-2.0 code + modified AI Pubs Open RAIL-M weights** (free for research/personal/startups under $5M funding-or-revenue; paid commercial otherwise — a real procurement decision), **not GPL-3.0**. Uzbek is covered: `static/docs/multilingual.md` lists `uz` at 88.9%. But Surya 2's OCR half **is itself a VLM requiring a running vllm/llama.cpp backend**, so "Surya instead of a VLM" is circular; only its **detector** (a modified EfficientViT with a segmentation decode head) is standalone torch.

**Why the conclusion survives anyway:**
1. Every published number above is **document** text. Ours is scene text over video: decorative fonts, low contrast, motion blur, gradient backgrounds, text over faces. No engine publishes a scene-text-on-video number for uz/ru, so an OCR-first pipeline would ship un-benchmarked — the failure this doc exists to prevent.
2. OCR gives characters; the tier needs a **judgement**. An OCR pass still needs a text classifier after it, so it adds a stage rather than replacing one — while a VL call answers directly at ~$0.0004–0.0007. The binding budget is wall clock, not dollars.
3. Real on-screen Uzbek Cyrillic is typed on Russian keyboards and already drops қ ў ғ ҳ (`config/campaigns/tashkent-renovation.md:237,321`: "канча = қанча", "тамир = таъмир"), so meaning-level judgement beats character-level fidelity regardless of dictionary. Note also that ТАЪМИР is not evidence of a gap — Т А Ъ М И Р are all standard Russian Cyrillic; only ҚАНЧА exercises it. And the okina point defuses the same way: PP-OCR's Latin dicts carry `'` `'` `'` but not U+02BB/U+02BC, which is a normalization problem Sheet #1's Remedy A.3 apostrophe-collapse already solves.

So, use OCR for the two jobs where the character dictionary does not matter:
1. **Detector-as-gate** — run only the DETECTION half (PP-OCR det, or Surya's detector) to answer "does this frame contain text, how much, where." Pure geometry, script-independent. Skip the VLM on textless frames and use it to select frames (Remedy F).
2. **OCR-as-verifier, offline only** — character overlap between the VLM's `read_text` (Remedy G) and an OCR read is a deterministic, reproducible, zero-label grounding signal complementing Remedy C. Configure it correctly (PaddleOCR with a Cyrillic lang code at PP-OCRv5, or EasyOCR `['tjk','ru']`), fold apostrophe/letter variants before comparing, and run it in `scripts/eval/`, **never on the hot path**.

No OCR dependency exists anywhere in the repo today (`grep paddleocr|easyocr|tesseract|surya` over `engine/`, `admin-panel/src`, `desktop/src-tauri/src` = zero hits) — all of this is greenfield.

**Effort:** 1 day for the verifier in the harness; 1–2 days for the detector gate on the hot path. **Risk:** medium — an OCR dependency in the worker sidecar is a real packaging cost (`desktop/pyinstaller/`), which is why the verifier goes first. A detector that errors must mean "send the frame," never "skip the reel."

## Remedy F — Frame policy: stop paying 3× for one picture

1. **Spread, don't burst.** 0.6s apart samples 1.2s of a 30–60s clip. Use the even-step `sample_frames` logic that already exists for the expensive tier (`core/media.py:135-154`), or at minimum widen the interval and take the first shot immediately after `open_reel` settles so the title card — what the Tashkent brief says carries everything — is captured deliberately rather than by luck.
2. **Dedupe before spending.** A perceptual hash (dHash, ~20 lines, no dep) over the captured frames; drop near-duplicates. On X image posts and LinkedIn carousels there is no `<video>` (`core/cdp.py:1010-1012` falls through to `page.screenshot`), so all three frames are near-identical today — this alone cuts those calls to 1/3.
3. **Bound the payload.** Pass `quality=` to the JPEG screenshot and downscale to the model's tile size before base64; pin `--window-size` in `scripts/warm_chrome.sh:393-397` and `worker/chrome_manager.py:379-382` so the token bill is a property of the code, not the monitor.
4. **Fix the mime.** Either write JPEGs from ffmpeg (`frame-%04d.jpg`, `core/media.py:108`) or detect the type in `frames_to_base64` — PNG bytes are currently labelled `data:image/jpeg` (`router.py:853`).
5. ⚠️ A format the policy must respect: the 2026 dominant short-form format is word-by-word karaoke captions synced to speech, so N frames from a burst give N fragments of one sentence — and that text is a transcript of the audio the STT tier separately pays for. Spread sampling and dedupe both help; so does telling the model (Remedy G) that fragmentary rolling captions are one utterance. *(Directional, from 2026 industry guidance retrieved 2026-08-21 — not a measurement.)*

**Effort:** 1–1.5 days. **Risk:** low-medium. Changing the frame count changes every measured number, so land this **before** the benchmark or the baseline key must be reissued — `evalstats.baseline_key` hashes the config for exactly this reason.

## Remedy G — Redesign the vision output contract: transcribe first, judge second

New contract:

```json
{"read_text": "<verbatim on-screen text across all frames, joined; \"\" if none legible>",
 "text_present": true,
 "subject": "<one noun phrase for what is shown>",
 "label": "relevant", "score": 0.0, "confidence": 0.0}
```

Three payoffs: (a) `read_text` is what Remedy B persists and what Remedy E's OCR verifier scores against — `reason` is doing this job by accident and gets truncated at 500 chars; (b) emitting the transcription **before** the verdict puts the grounded tokens first, which matters because visual conditioning decays across generated tokens (⚠️ arXiv:2509.10345); (c) `text_present=false` is a first-class **abstention** the cascade can act on, replacing the "use a borderline score (0.40-0.55)" convention that every vision prompt states in prose, nothing enforces, and the confidence tie-break at `cascade.py:272` silently converts into a win. Sheet #1's `UNKNOWN`-is-a-verdict rule is the same principle.

Then fix the two places the contract is contradicted: give the vision call its own user-message template instead of the hard-coded "Read the on-screen text across these N frame(s)" at `router.py:846-849` (which double-instructs the video tier on top of `_video_instruction`), and teach the vision system prompt that a `SPOKEN TEXT` block may be present so a textless-but-narrated reel is not told to abstain.

⚠️ arXiv:2603.19790 (v1 2026-03-20, v4 2026-07-30) is the formal version of the abstention argument — withhold transcriptions lacking coherent cross-view evidence, on the grounds that "erroneous but fluent text output can be more costly than abstention"; its cross-view probe fits naturally here since we already hold multiple frames of one item. Fetched 2026-08-21; **re-verify.**

**Effort:** 2 days. **Risk:** medium. Changing the contract invalidates any generated `visionPrompt` already stored on a live campaign, so `_prompt_carries_contract` must be extended in the same change (Remedy H) and stored prompts predating it treated as legacy, not silently mis-parsed. `_has_usable_verdict` (`router.py:253-273`) stays the parse gate and needs no change.

## Remedy H — Fix the generator so the vision prompt it writes is a vision prompt

1. **Per-key validation instead of one shared predicate.** `_prompt_carries_contract` (`campaign_gen.py:883-889`) becomes `_PROMPT_VALIDATORS[key]`; the vision validator additionally requires frame/on-screen-text vocabulary and the `read_text`/`text_present` keys. A relevance prompt pasted under `visionPrompt` must fail.
2. **Pass `languageMix` and the campaign's script list into `_advanced_prompts_user`** (`:892-900`), and have `SYSTEM_CAMPAIGN_PROMPTS` (`core/prompts.py:138-153`) require the vision prompt to name the scripts it will meet and the orthographic variance within them. Sheet #1 already built `discovery/translit.py`, whose Cyrillic/Latin/apostrophe knowledge can be templated in **deterministically** rather than asked for.
3. **Raise or drop the 1200-character cap for the vision key.** The prompt that demonstrably works is 4,261 characters and its value is entirely in the enumerated hard negatives.
4. **Ask explicitly for the hard-negative list** — "name 5-8 things in this market that share the campaign's KEYWORD or its price shape but are a different purchase." That is the single highest-value section of the Tashkent prompt and no current instruction elicits it.
5. Optionally template the live gate value into the rubric the way `ig_match(threshold)` does, so the vision prose and `RELEVANCE_GATE` cannot drift.

Add `X_VISION` and `LINKEDIN_VISION` (modelled on `IG_VISION`) in the same change, or those two engines keep sending a caption prompt to a camera.

**Effort:** 1–1.5 days. **Risk:** low, and it **fails safe** — a stricter validator drops more generated prompts, and a dropped prompt falls back to `IG_VISION`/`VISION_GENERIC`, i.e. the status quo. Surface the drop, or it reads to the operator as "the AI stopped filling in the Advanced section."

## Remedy I — Human spot-check: 40 items, 90 minutes, once

Once Remedy B is persisting read-outs, sample 40 reels stratified by (vision fired / did not) × (vision agreed / flipped the text verdict) and have the operator answer two questions per item with the reel open: (1) is the read-out text actually on screen (grounding: yes/no/partial), (2) is the final verdict right. Forty items with Wilson intervals distinguishes "roughly right" from "broken" — the only question worth asking before investing in a real gold set — and it calibrates Remedy C's automated grounding metric against a human, which is what makes the automated metric trustworthy enough to run unattended. Sheet #3's own arithmetic keeps it honest: on 25 items a precision of 0.80 carries a 95% interval of roughly 0.59–0.93, so a 40-item pass is a smoke test and must be reported as one. Escalate to a 150–200 item vision gold set only if the spot check or Remedy C says the tier is actually deciding something.

**Effort:** 0.5 day engineering + ~90 min operator time. **Risk:** low. The one discipline that matters: the labeller must not see the model's verdict first.

## Remedy J — The cost question, answered

**Money is not the constraint.** ⚠️ At `qwen/qwen3-vl-32b-instruct` ($0.104/M in, $0.416/M out, live 2026-08-21), a browser-screenshot frame under Qwen3-VL's **patch-16 / 2×2-merge** scheme costs `H*W/1024` tokens — for a typical desktop `<video>` box (~500×900) ~440 tokens; for a full 1080×1920 frame ~2,025. Three frames plus an 841-char system prompt (`IG_VISION`; `VISION_GENERIC` is 651) is ~1,600–6,400 input and ~120 output ⇒ **$0.0002–$0.0007 per gated reel**, ~$0.0009–$0.0018 for the 8-frame video tier (`AIZU_VIDEO_FRAMES` default 8, `instagram/cdp.py:329`). A thousand reels/day is 20–70 cents.

⚠️ The exact figure is **unknowable today** because nothing fixes the frame size: `_shoot` screenshots the rendered `<video>` element and there is no viewport configuration anywhere in `core/cdp.py` or `instagram/cdp.py`. Note also this is a per-RUN cost while the umbrella study's ≤$1 is a per-campaign-CREATION budget — different ledgers. Either way the order of magnitude settles it: "OCR is cheaper" is not an argument at this scale. Measure it directly the first time a real call succeeds — `usage.cost` comes back on the response and `_cost_from_usage` prefers it over the fallback table (`router.py:434-449`).

**And today it is literally zero, which is the actual problem.** The shipped default is free, and `_record` writes a spend_log row only when `usd > 0` (`router.py:636`) — so under the default model every vision call costs nothing and leaves no trace. The tier is free and invisible, not expensive.

**Wall clock is already handled** — see "What is NOT wrong" above. Do not build against it.

**The correctness cost is the unmeasured one.** A wrong vision verdict wins the tie-break at `cascade.py:272` (`>=`, so vision wins *equal* confidence), and on the thin-caption path it is the sole judgment with no text verdict to overrule it. One such error drops a real lead source or admits a car-repair reel into a renovation campaign, and costs more than every vision call the run will ever make. So the honest verdict for this sheet is not "amber, un-benchmarked" but: the tier is **mis-configured** (Remedy A), its output is **un-persisted** (Remedy B), and its verdict is **un-attributed** (no counter, no stage tag, no ledger row) — three defects that must be fixed before "does the prompt work" is even askable.

**Effort:** instrumentation folded into A and B; no standalone build.

## Deliberately excluded

- **Vendoring a scraped image gold set** — no `.png/.jpg` exists here today and none should. Downloading a public file transfers no rights; Meta's licence runs to Meta; third-party downloader terms uniformly forbid dataset-building. The product is local-first: frames stay in memory (they already do — `capture_video_frames` sweeps its `MediaWorkdir` on exit, `engines/instagram/cdp.py:311-341`) and the persisted artefact is DERIVED TEXT (`ocr_text`) plus a perceptual hash, which is not a reproduction. If frames must be retained at all they stay operator-local behind an explicit opt-in with a deletion TTL — never in git, never in CI, never in a shared fixture directory. Same reasoning as Sheet #1's refusal to vendor a scraped banned-tag blocklist.
- **Tesseract as the primary reader** — it is the only engine with real uz-Cyrillic weights, which is exactly why it must be said out loud: it is a *document* OCR engine and this input is scene text. Using it as the classifier's eyes trades a VLM error for an OCR error the downstream text classifier cannot recover from, because stage-1 character errors are unrecoverable in a two-stage pipeline.
- **Synthetic rendered frames as the gold set** — cheap, legally clean, and measures the wrong thing. Synthetic text is clean, axis-aligned, high-contrast and correctly spelled; every failure mode that matters (decorative fonts, Cyrillic typed on a Russian keyboard, `ta'mir/taʼmir/tamir`, karaoke fragments, a phone number over a dark room) is absent. Useful only as a **negative control**: failing on synthetic frames proves the prompt is broken; passing proves nothing. Sheet #3's rule applies — synthetic only to fill strata, different model family, 100% human-verified.
- **A separate vision benchmark harness** — Sheet #3 already built the pieces (`core/evalstats.py`) and the store-less real-router replay works today with `OpenRouterRouter(store=None)`. Vision is one more variant dimension, not a second harness. Reuse also inherits its two hard-won traps: one router per variant, abort on degraded runs.
- **Fine-tuning a VLM, or training a CLIP/embedding classifier on frames** — both need the image corpus we deliberately refuse to build, both are unfalsifiable below ~1,000 labelled items, and neither is reachable before A and B have produced a single real vision verdict. Revisit only if Remedy D's pseudo-gold grows past four figures.
- **Cloud document-OCR APIs on the hot path** (Google Cloud Vision, Yandex Vision, Mistral OCR) — a second vendor credential, a second failure mode, a second rate limit, and per-page pricing that is not obviously below what a VL call now costs. ⚠️ Yandex claims 50+ languages but I could not confirm Uzbek or current pricing (searched 2026-08-21), and adding a Russian-cloud dependency to a Tashkent-market product is an operator decision. Same posture Sheet #1 took on Reddit OAuth and Wordstat: real, deferred, credential-gated.
- **Raising the frame count as a cure for low signal** — three near-identical frames are already the problem; more of them multiplies tokens and latency without adding information. The fix is spread + dedupe. The 8-frame video tier already sits behind a per-campaign flag AND a global kill-switch (`enable_video_analysis` + `AIZU_VIDEO_ANALYSIS_ENABLED`, `cascade.py:299-300`) and that gating is correct — leave it.
- **Model-comparison fan-out for vision** (`model_comparison_log`) — Sheet #3 established its `agreed` column is NULL for every row ever written and the fix is blocked on a `core/router.py` change. Extending a known-broken instrument to a second stage adds rows nobody can read.
- **k-sampled voting on the vision verdict** — same wall as Sheet #3's Remedy F: `_CLASSIFY_BUDGET_SEC = 80.0` is one allowance for ONE logical classification and a single vision call can consume it. Threading a separate budget through `classify_image` reintroduces the multiplication bug that dead-lettered `job-2099fb29e88b`. If a second opinion is ever needed it is a different MODEL on the same budget, not the same model k times.
- **Routing vision around `_HeartbeatRouter`** — the facade (`instagram/session.py:91` + twins) wraps `classify_image` as well as `classify_text`. Any new vision call site — the ablation arm, the pseudo-gold capture, an OCR-verified re-ask — must go THROUGH it, or the 180s watchdog halts the run. Noted because two remedies above add call sites.

## Open questions

1. **Which vision model is the operator ACTUALLY running?** No `.env` is in the tree, and the diagnosis branches on it: if `OPENROUTER_VISION_MODEL` is overridden to a live id, the tier has merely never been measured; if not, it has never returned a verdict. One log line from a live box settles it, and nothing else should be built until it is settled.
2. **Does `_shoot` return a real video frame or a black rectangle?** `scripts/warm_chrome.sh:393-397` launches headful Chrome with GPU compositing and no `--disable-gpu`/`--use-gl=swiftshader`, and `_shoot` screenshots the `<video>` element. On macOS a hardware-overlay-composited video can be excluded from `Page.captureScreenshot`. **This is the cheapest experiment in the sheet** — dump one `_shoot()` result to a PNG and look at it — and if it fails, every other remedy is moot. Do it first.
3. **Is the Tashkent campaign as stored in the DB carrying the file's 4,261-char vision prompt, or is `vision_prompt` blank** so the run falls through to `IG_VISION`? `_BRIEF_BLANK_DROP_KEYS` (`server.py:853`) drops blank prompt keys and `campaign_briefs` is the live source — the file on disk may not be what runs. One query.
4. **Is `RELEVANCE_GATE = 0.5` meant to be per-campaign?** It is a module constant in six files while `campaign.threshold` is panel-editable, and every vision prompt hard-codes 0.50 in prose. Making it a campaign field fixes two diagnoses together; leaving it constant means the prompts should stop restating it.
5. **Will the operator accept keeping frames on the box at all**, even opt-in with a TTL? B, C and D need only derived text, but the human spot-check is much faster with a thumbnail than a reel URL. Product/legal call.
6. **How many reels per session actually reach the vision tier?** `used_vision` is discarded and the run logs are all dry-run, so the firing rate is unknowable — which also means nobody can say whether fixing the `_unsure` cutoff makes vision fire 3× more often or 30×. Remedy B's counter answers it in one live run.
7. **Do the STT tier and the vision tier read the same words?** If the dominant format is speech-synced burned-in captions, transcript and on-screen text are the same content bought twice at two budgets, and the correct design may be to run one and skip the other rather than chain them (`cascade.py:275-313` chains). Remedy B's persisted `ocr_text` beside the existing `transcript` column makes this a SQL query on the first live run.
